newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan big banks' operating profits seen down.
newsitem.headline: Japan big banks' operating profits seen down.

text.p: Operating profits at Japan's 10 biggest commercial banks are expected to fall in the current financial year, partly due to lower profits from bond sales, the chairman of the Federation of Bankers' Associations of Japan said on Tuesday.
The 1996/97 financial year ends in March.

Shunsaku Hashimoto, who is also president of Sakura Bank Ltd, one of the nation's biggest banks, told reporters that plans to separate the Finance Ministry's inspection and supervisory functions seemed to be gaining support.
Japanese politicians are currently working on bills to reform the Finance Ministry, which has been criticised for its lax handling of the banking industry.

Hashimoto said the Finance Ministry's planning and supervisory functions are different from the inspection function. "If inspection is to be separated (from the supervisory function), it is important to consider how to maintain closer relations between the inspection function and the planning and supervisory functions," he said.

Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said earlier this month that the government would aim to have its bills on ministry reforms pass through parliament at the next regular session, which begins in January.
The ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) and the Social Democratic and Sakigake parties have agreed to spin off the supervisory function of the Finance Ministry into an independent body.
A ministry source said recently that MOF wants a bank inspection body that is semi-independent and not totally outside its jurisdiction.

On the banks' forecast earnings, Hashimoto said: "When we see the commercial banks' earnings on an annual basis, operating profits are expected to be lower (for 1996/97) from a year earlier because of a decline in profits from bond sales and (low) interest rates."

Last Friday, the 10 biggest commercial banks announced their interim earnings. Their combined operating profits -- pre-tax profits from banking business -- fell 36 percent from a year earlier to 1.19 trillion yen in the first half of 1996/97.
